decisions.disposition: advance research nomination; lead
decisions.evidence_scope: Prior niacin muscle NAD evidence plus primary qualification of actual nicotinic-acid toxicant co-protection in oocytes; intervention, tissue and sirtuin distinctions retained.
decisions.rationale: The open-label strength changes do not establish disease-specific rescue; [study details and control strategy](track2-evidence-pipeline.md#why-this-pair-and-what-remains-to-be-proved). The SIRT2 survival result was genetic; NMN abundance experiments were a different intervention. Niacin/N1002K rescue has not been demonstrated in the reviewed evidence. A [pediatric MTTN case](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39173541/) progressed despite NAD correction. The [prescription label](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/fda/fdaDrugXsl.cfm?setid=dd60fe81-3d54-4a29-9502-601be89c575e) does not establish pediatric safety/effectiveness. A 2025 primary nicotinic-acid co-treatment study reports partial human-oocyte maturation protection from benzo(a)pyrene. Figure 4 gives means 56.7% drug+toxin, 31.7% toxin,73.5% control, but no direct drug-versus-toxin significance label. Mouse SIRT1 experiments, not SIRT2; no direct NAD measurement, drug-induced BUBR1 restoration or MVA muscle outcome. This strengthens a distinct actual-compound cellular precedent without closing the proposed mechanism bridge.

decisions.disposition: retain downstream mechanism-probe arm
decisions.evidence_scope: Previously reviewed route rationale; grouping does not establish identical drug-specific effects.
decisions.rationale: Two mice/genotype, no total-substrate denominators, quantification or inferential test: increased pathway activity is unestablished. Carrier findings do not establish biallelic MVA1 signaling or drug rescue. X753 differs from L737Ter; mouse L1002P models human L1012P, not N1002K. [Baker's rapamycin nonbenefit](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3785294/) is a parenthetical unpublished observation, without a treatment figure or complete regimen. [Goutas 2023](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10149375/), Fig. 6, found BUBR1 loss after 50 nM everolimus for 24 hours in late-passage WJ-MSCs, not early-passage cells.

decisions.disposition: within-class reference, reserve implementation
decisions.evidence_scope: Previously reviewed route rationale; grouping does not establish identical drug-specific effects. Separate primary renal study qualified with exact schedule, endpoint and tissue distinctions.
decisions.rationale: The published fly study reports rapamycin feeding improving neuroblast counts. Genetic autophagy/TOR interventions did not restore progeny counts or brain size; drug and genetic endpoint sets must remain separate. This is a different checkpoint lesion and neural tissue, not BUB1B muscle. The BubR1 mouse negative observation was an unpublished parenthetical, not a fully reported treatment trial. No comparative MVA superiority established. Separately, rapamycin preserved weight-normalized creatinine clearance and reduced proteinuria/adhesions in AA-4E-BP1 transgenic rats after nephrectomy. Alternate-day exposure had significant functional effects with slowed body growth; weekly exposure did not significantly improve those three endpoints. Bulk glomerular Bub1b RNA decreased during protection, without a BUBR1 protein or per-cell measurement. This is actual-drug renal evidence in another lesion, not MVA or muscle rescue, and cannot be assigned to everolimus.

decisions.disposition: mechanistic and mixed controlled human-function comparator; not an established approved-drug submission lead
decisions.evidence_scope: Previously qualified North evidence plus complete Kang main-text and six figure-legend reading through NCBI BioC; Kang figure pixels, supplements and movies unreviewed. No numeric rescue estimate or exact Figure 4F denominator claimed. New two-trial human qualification: complete Yi 2023 and Igarashi 2026 scientific mains, key native figures/tables and complete supplements; current NCT and first/current jRCT records. Original North/Kang reading limits remain unchanged. Separate Igarashi 2022 qualification: complete scientific main and supplementary-table text, all native main figures/tables, selected native supplementary tables, public Reporting Summary custom fields, all three official UMIN versions and bounded notices; full protocol/SAP and raw participant data not recovered.
decisions.rationale: North provides WT BUBR1 abundance evidence at high experimental exposure. Separately, Kang 2018 reports 0.5 mM NMN improving mitotic completion in NQO1-depleted MCF-7 cancer cells. That is functional division evidence, not niacin treatment, BUBR1-loss rescue, faithful daughter chromosome counts or muscle function. Genetic SIRT2 survival benefits remain separate. Product eligibility and actual-allele benefit at justified exposure remain unestablished. Oral NMN also has qualified randomized human functional evidence: Yi 2023 randomized 80 healthy adults to AbinoNutra NMN 300/600/900 mg daily or pooled placebo for 60 days and reports favorable between-group changes in manual-treadmill six-minute walking. Figure 2B supplies the nominal treatment comparisons; within-arm P values are different. No model-adjusted meter estimate, contrast CI or broad multiplicity correction is supplied, and registry endpoint hierarchy, discussion and supplemental labels have unresolved inconsistencies. Igarashi 2026, an Article in Press, randomized 62 older adults to MIRAILAB NMN 1,250 mg/day or placebo for 24 weeks; 30/28 had week-24 measurements. Registered secondary grip, chair, gait and hallway-walking results were nonpositive despite increased whole-blood NAD+. One active participant discontinued for liver-enzyme increases; the native post-stop plot shows AST rising while ALT falls slightly, contrary to prose suggesting improvement or no further increases, and causality remains uncertain. These trials strengthen NMN as a mixed controlled human-function comparator to niacin's uncontrolled functional observations without establishing head-to-head superiority, an optimal dose, MVA efficacy or product eligibility. No selective requirement for MVA rescue is imposed on NMN; the reciprocal function, renewal and fidelity criterion remains unchanged. A separately qualified Igarashi 2022 trial randomized 42 healthy older men to Mitsubishi-supplied oral NMN 250 mg/day or placebo for 12 weeks. A dispensing error at week six gave the opposite supplement to 11 participants per arm, and their 22 week-12 datasets were excluded; baseline and six-week observations from all 42 participants remained. Nominal longitudinal gait and left-grip interactions and the full-cohort six-week chair-change comparison (ANCOVA P=.031) deserve credit. The highlighted week-12 gait endpoint P=.002 comes from only 20 retained participants with baseline gait imbalance; its change comparison is P=.066, not .002. Registered primary skeletal muscle index was nonpositive; functional outcomes were not listed in the accessible original registry, and all analyses were exploratory without multiplicity correction. Retained-subset lean-mass contrasts favoring placebo also remain, without implying general muscle harm. Whole-blood NAD engagement was measured, not muscle BUBR1 rescue. This adds another qualified motor signal with substantial exposure and analysis limits; it does not establish a preferred dose, formulation, MVA efficacy or superiority over niacin. The previously qualified trials and reciprocal research criteria remain unchanged.

decisions.disposition: substantive preliminary human-function comparator; restoration unproved
decisions.evidence_scope: Earlier NR metabolic counterevidence retained; full scientific main and selected supplement/protocol/registry qualification of the NICE randomized PAD trial. A separately qualified NEM6 mouse study adds preventive mitochondrial morphology/protein context with no direct respiratory treatment test or treated strength/endurance result; a DMD functional-null abstract remains separate.
decisions.rationale: NICE randomized 90 older adults with PAD to NR 1,000 mg/day, NR plus trans-resveratrol, or placebo for six months. NR improved the assigned-group six-minute-walk contrast by 17.6 m (one-sided 90% CI +1.8 to infinity; P=.08), meeting the supplied pilot one-sided P<.10 rule without multiplicity correction. This is a real controlled functional signal, not conventional two-sided 5% confirmatory evidence or a 17.6-m within-arm gain. Sparse biopsies did not demonstrate muscle NAD benefit; BUBR1 and checkpoint rescue were not measured. The adherence-selected larger effect is post-hoc. Existing 40-man obese/insulin-resistant 2,000-mg/day metabolic null remains, but cannot erase the different PAD result. NR now merits a substantive human-function comparison with niacin, without established MVA superiority, pediatric safety or product-level approved-drug eligibility. Earlier Elhassan muscle-metabolome engagement (NAAD/clearance metabolites) remains distinct from an increased NAD pool or force rescue. In NEM6 mice, NR chloride from four weeks for eight weeks accompanies fewer severely damaged mitochondria and selected OXPHOS-subunit increases. Respiratory comparisons test genotype within separate untreated/treated cohorts, each normalized to its own WT; loss of genotype significance is not a demonstrated treatment effect. Placebo-controlled allocation, post-treatment NAD, treated grip/endurance and BUBR1 responses are absent or unreported. This supports a preventive organelle hypothesis, not another demonstrated functional rescue. A separate complete DMD abstract reports no sustainable NAD expansion or hindlimb-force protection with NR under eccentric challenge; its dose and full methods remain unqualified. The NICE-based functional priority is unchanged.

decisions.evidence_scope: Prior BUBR1 abundance rationale plus distinct Bub3 marker study; nicotinamide and nicotinic acid remain separate.
decisions.rationale: It is not nicotinic acid. North's high-dose nicotinamide reduced BUBR1, consistent with sirtuin inhibition; that does not establish that every concentration is harmful. No useful BUBR1 rescue window established. A separate Bub3 study tests 5 mM NAM for 12 h: increased crotonylation, with SIRT1-knockdown support; chromosome-error measurements belong to genetic mutants. This does not show NAM-induced segregation errors or harm from nicotinic acid.

In [11 older people with probable sarcopenia](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40100528/), four weeks produced no significant muscle-NAD increase or secondary benefit.

decisions.disposition: upgrade combination-specific contracture-compensation reserve; do not elect single-medicine lead
decisions.evidence_scope: Complete neonatal-denervation primary article and supplement, with independent treatment/figure checks; older MG132, tumor and labeling evidence remains separately scoped.
decisions.rationale: Bortezomib plus [Gly14]-Humanin G prevented contractures and preserved longitudinal muscle growth after neonatal denervation. Passive joint range was assessed blinded after sacrifice; this is functional prevention credit, not active force, reinnervation or established-contracture reversal. All drug arms included humanin, so neither bortezomib-alone efficacy nor a protective contribution from humanin is isolated. Optimized treatment still had mortality and significantly reduced normally innervated muscle area/volume. Reused earlier-start controls, uncertain enrollment/attrition and missing relevant-exposure, long-term function and developmental safety limit election. Separate MG132 protein preservation/alignment results do not establish faithful completed divisions or transfer to bortezomib. The pediatric bortezomib/vorinostat trial does not establish BUB1B selectivity; no starting renal adjustment is not proof of safety in nephrocalcinosis.

Gentamicin's kidney/hearing liabilities constrain use. [Ataluren EU authorization was not renewed in 2025](https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/medicines/human/EPAR/translarna) after efficacy remained unconfirmed; this does not falsify the entire mechanism.

decisions.disposition: selective-clearance research reserve, decline current medication lead
decisions.evidence_scope: Human platelet toxicity; separate mouse neurovascular/cognitive benefit and chemotherapy-pretreated T-ALL challenge counterexample. Targeted 2025 actual-drug normalized-grip and attrition check, separate from genetic GCV clearance. Additional named sources are complete saved-abstract re-readings only, documented in umk57-qualification.md.
decisions.rationale: Baker used INK-ATTAC/AP20187, not navitoclax. [Human phase I experience](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4979082/) found platelet toxicity with intermittent as well as continuous exposure; sparing megakaryocytes does not establish survival of BCL-XL-dependent platelets. No pediatric MVA senolytic pulse schedule or approved-product eligibility was established here. A separate paclitaxel mouse study reports neurovascular/BBB/cognitive benefit; measured muscle tests had no injury deficit to rescue. Navitoclax worsened a distinct chemotherapy-pretreated minimal-cell T-ALL challenge. Timing/dose discrepancies and tumor-context limits remain unresolved; no MVA benefit or universal harm is inferred. A separate 2025 old-mouse navitoclax (ABT-263) experiment adds a normalized-grip benefit (printed 3.34 +/- 0.21, n=8, versus 2.55 +/- 0.19, n=14, g force/g body weight, p=0.0172), not an absolute-force or MVA rescue. Dose, attrition and cross-study comparisons require caution: the reported 23 percent gain disagrees with the ratio of the printed means, which is about 31 percent, so the percentage is not promoted here. Eight old mice died before baseline, two during vehicle dosing and six during navitoclax dosing; attributing those deaths to age does not establish absence of drug harm. A separate abstract (PMID26188358) reports that ABT-263 added to Oxindole-1 or ZM447439 enhances loss of viability in AML lines and primary blasts; Bcl-xL knockdown, unlike Bcl-2 knockdown, reproduced the combination effect. Credit that antitumor result without transferring it to single-agent muscle benefit or assuming constitutional aneuploid cells share the same dependency. Nonmalignant-tissue effects and exposure remain open.

decisions.disposition: distinct conditional reserve
decisions.evidence_scope: Previously reviewed route rationale; grouping does not establish identical drug-specific effects.
decisions.rationale: Suppressing harmful secretions is different from killing cells. Neither study demonstrates ruxolitinib rescue of developmental BUB1B disease or proves that JAK-dependent secretions cause its muscle defect. Xu's broader secretion/conditioned-medium experiments used JAK inhibitor 1; they cannot all be assigned to ruxolitinib. The [drug label](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/fda/fdaDrugXsl.cfm?setid=f1c82580-87ae-11e0-bc84-0002a5d5c51b) adds cytopenia, infection and developmental-exposure constraints.

decisions.rationale: Tang's BUBR1-low experiment tested AICAR/17-AAG, not chloroquine; chloroquine did not suppress the tested human CIN/MIN lines. Goutas measured abundance, not restored function, at high culture exposure. [Chloroquine](https://www.dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=f4ac1556-0522-76e3-e053-2a95a90a5ba8) and [hydroxychloroquine](https://www.dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=f2002851-852f-4ee8-e053-2a95a90a242d) labels warn about muscle weakness/myopathy, particularly relevant to this objective.

decisions.disposition: decline muscle nomination; retain metformin-specific protein-stability lead; AICAR remains a separate declined lead
decisions.evidence_scope: Prior MASTERS clinical-muscle appraisal and AICAR abstract findings retained; metformin TET2 paper now qualified from complete main text, Methods, main/Extended Data legends, key pixels and supplementary methods.
decisions.rationale: Antiproliferation is not muscle rescue. [MASTERS randomized trial](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6826125/) found metformin blunted resistance-training muscle hypertrophy in older adults. That result does not settle pediatric MVA, but opposes an assumed anabolic benefit. AICAR reference experiments cannot be assigned to metformin. The re-read AICAR abstract (PMID21315436) reports p53-mediated apoptosis in MEFs trisomic for chromosomes 1, 13, 16 or 19, and AICAR/17-AAG activity, especially combined, in aneuploid human cancer lines. No result transfers to metformin or establishes an MVA tissue-preservation window. Separately, complete primary qualification of metformin (PMID30022161) establishes a positive TET2-stabilization mechanism with downstream cancer-model outcomes. In high-glucose A2058 cells genetically restored with full-length TET2-WT, 5 mM metformin slowed protein decay, increased 5hmC and reduced growth; 2-4 mM reduced soft-agar colonies. Drinking-water metformin (500 mg/L), begun seven days before implantation, additionally suppressed WT xenograft growth in diabetic and nondiabetic mice. Mock, S99A and TET2-knockdown controls limited the effects in the tested systems; the drug did not substitute for genetic target restoration. The authors acknowledge up to 5 mM cell exposure versus approximately 20 micromolar human circulation. Actual consumed mouse dose/plasma exposure are unknown; final n=4-5 versus Methods n=6 remains unexplained. The design tests pretreatment/early growth, not regression of established tumors. The separate A769662 stabilization result does not belong to metformin. Retain this favorable protein-specific mechanism without erasing MASTERS or transferring AICAR effects, and without claiming BUBR1 restoration, faithful division, muscle benefit or MVA efficacy. Patient phase and Asn1002Lys function/abundance remain unresolved.

decisions.disposition: redox reserve, decline lead
decisions.evidence_scope: Prior redox/meiotic and clinical comparisons plus qualified preventive retinal-cell marker/SASP evidence; not a second NAC drug entry.
decisions.rationale: No demonstrated BUB1B-dependent redox cause or rescue. The [randomized RYR1-myopathy trial](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7274912/) failed its primary oxidative-stress endpoint and did not establish a functional benefit. It is a different myopathy but stronger than a generic antioxidant rationale. In Sod1-null oocytes, NAC and ascorbate reduced premature sister-chromatid separation and improved normal-chromosome outcomes; distinct lesion and meiotic tissue, without demonstrated BUBR1 mediation or muscle rescue. In ARPE-19 cells,1mM NAC during smoke/peroxide insult partially prevented senescence-associated beta-galactosidase and inflammatory secretion. No delayed-start rescue or retinal-function result; VEGF/CFH and p16/p21 panels lack NAC arms.

decisions.disposition: Prioritize assay and exposure clarification for an access-limited functional/BUB1b lead; medication rank unresolved
decisions.evidence_scope: Complete exact official abstract and identity/access metadata read; scientific main, Methods, supplements and native figures remain inaccessible. No full-primary or new outer-reading credit.
decisions.rationale: The exact abstract reports icariin at 100 mg/kg once daily for 15 days in 24-month-old mice, with improved motor coordination/learning and rotarod score. BUB1b is named among significantly upregulated markers, but RNA versus protein, assay, tissue, effect size and biological n remain unverified. Route, vehicle, supplier and purity are unresolved. Fecal transfer from icariin-treated old donors, and separately from young donors, has reported functional benefit; these are distinct interventions from directly administered icariin and do not establish an isolated ingredient effect, exclusive microbiome mediation or BUB1B dependence. Nulls, harms, cage/donor clustering, randomization and blinding cannot be resolved from the abstract. Retain the functional claim without assigning verified BubR1 protein restoration, a wild-type genotype from unread Methods, human/MVA efficacy, or equivalence to Epimedium extracts and retail products.

decisions.disposition: Formulation-unresolved neuroprotective reserve with BUB1B molecular response
decisions.evidence_scope: Partial exact-source qualification: official abstract, complete authenticated supplement and native main Figures1–5; scientific main/Methods and main captions inaccessible. Not an all-literature efficacy assessment.
decisions.rationale: VK2 pretreatment before neonatal surgery/fentanyl/sevoflurane exposures protected P30 behavior and accompanied recovery of NAc Bub1b mRNA and BUB1B-labeled normalized immunofluorescence (S3:3 mice/group). This exceeds hub membership alone but does not establish functional BubR1 per-cell restoration, stabilization, causal dependence or MVA rescue; altered tissue composition may contribute. decisions.route: STLC and monastrol / Eg5 force balancing
decisions.disposition: conditional motor-force comparator; whole-population fidelity unresolved
decisions.rationale: Actual inhibitors shorten delayed mitosis and partly improve fibers after HMMR depletion. Timing analysis selects cells already having aligned chromosomes and normal bipolar spindles; mispositioning persists. Main/supplemental concentrations differ. Genetic chromosome counts cannot establish drug-treated faithful output. A separate LIC-depletion study actually uses STLC: depleted frog embryos gain bipolar spindles but retain abnormal categories, while depleted HeLaM cells lose bipolar prevalence and become predominantly monopolar. Control cells/embryos also become predominantly monopolar. Fixed distributions do not track individual cell transitions; these are lesion/model-specific structural effects, not completed faithful divisions. A separate CENP-W-depleted HeLa experiment used monastrol at 100 micromolar for the final 4 hours of a 48-hour siRNA transfection: supernumerary centrosomal foci (Figure 4B) and abnormal centriole splitting (Figure 5A) fell in CENP-W-depleted cells. The bipolarity observation runs the other way. The authors report that CENP-W depletion counteracts monastrol's monopolar arrest, with over 50% of observed mitotic spindles apparently bipolar under the combined perturbation, against more than 90% of monastrol-treated control cells showing two adjacent centriole pairs at the centre of a monopolar spindle. No bipolar rate is reported for CENP-W depletion without monastrol, so the drug is not shown to add bipolarity to the lesion, and that observation must not be listed as a third drug benefit. Fixed snapshots do not establish completed faithful descendants; this lesion accumulates BubR1 rather than modeling BUBR1 insufficiency. A distinct published CENP-E feedback study (PMID41120338) uses monastrol as an actual negative mechanistic control: forced transient monopolarization followed by washout and CENP-E inhibition did not reproduce the reduced polar chromosome burden near acentriolar poles. General Methods specify monastrol 100 micromolar for 3 hours or acutely as noted; a separate acute spindle-shortening experiment uses 50 micromolar. Spindle shortening is measured, not a useful-cell rescue. This source does not test STLC and adds no BubR1 or postdivision-fidelity benefit.

decisions.disposition: retain mechanistic comparator; decline current medication lead
decisions.rationale: In DNA-PKcs-deficient cells challenged with nocodazole, 12 micromolar proTAME raises selected mitotic substrates and phosphorylation signals, quantified across three separate experiments with abundance normalized to Ku80 and phosphosignals to their own total protein. In HeLa (Figure 7) proTAME significantly raised anillin, cyclin B1, securin, Aurora A pT288, PLK1 pT210 and TPX2 pS121. In A549 (Figure 8) only anillin, cyclin B1, securin and TPX2 pS121 rose significantly; PLK1 pT210 was unchanged on both normalizations, and Aurora A pT288 relative to total Aurora A was significantly lower under proTAME than in untreated deficient cells, from a baseline not significantly different from DNA-PKcs-proficient controls. The paper cites panels 8F, 8G, 8I and 8J as rescue evidence; those panels do not show it. Anillin in A549 overshoots the proficient control. This is a direction reversal on an Aurora-A activation marker, not merely a smaller effect. proTAME was administered only to DNA-PKcs-deficient cells and only under nocodazole: there is no proficient-genotype drug arm and no arm in which a spindle could form. Because APC/C inhibition is unconditional while BUBR1 restraint is attachment-conditional, preserved securin and cyclin B1 are the signature of maintained mitotic arrest, not of corrected division. Bulk arrested-cell lysates do not establish per-cell checkpoint correction, BUBR1 restoration, faithful descendants or muscle output. The probe is retained for the APC/C node, not as a route to restore faithful division; a washout experiment producing more absolute faithful daughters would be the test that could overturn that reading. proTAME is a research-tool prodrug supplied in the saved source as a DMSO reagent stock, with no match in the saved 14,882-entity clinical and approval catalog and no human exposure in the reviewed record. It is not eligible as a repurposing candidate; it is retained only as a mechanism probe.

That inertness is a HeLa statement: in A549 apcin significantly lowered total Aurora A, Aurora A pT288, PLK1 pT210 and TPX2 pS121 below the untreated deficient condition, so it is not inert there but suppressive. The saved source's own no-effect summary does not cover A549. The combination of proTAME and apcin returns the panels to the deficient level or below, but no panel reports a combination-versus-proTAME-alone comparison; every bracket anchors to the deficient plus nocodazole bar, and the combination outcome appears only in the Discussion. Antagonism is therefore isolated only in HeLa, and in A549 apcin's own suppression competes with antagonism as the explanation. Alternative degradation is an author-proposed hypothesis, not a demonstrated mediator. This is context-specific biochemical counterevidence, not proof of universal inefficacy or toxicity, and no MVA muscle benefit or therapeutic window is established. Apcin is a research tool with no match in the previously reviewed saved clinical and approval catalog; the context-specific negative findings remain relevant mechanistic comparators. This establishes context-dependent direction, not a response in this patient or an effect of proTAME. A second abstract (PMID26423134) reports increased apcin response in cohesion-defective WABS and cancer cells; the study describes checkpoint-dependent synthetic lethality. Genetic and drug arms require full-text separation. Neither abstract establishes faithful division or MVA muscle benefit; this child cannot be assumed to lack all checkpoint function. Separately, Shi et al. (PMID36911196) administered Apcin at 30 mg/kg intraperitoneally eight hours before CCl4 injury in mice. Plotted survival improved and ALT/AST decreased. The survival plot ends around day four despite a stated seven-day endpoint; no survival significance statistic is reported. Caption n=4 for ALT/AST does not resolve biological versus technical repeats. Injury-associated expression comparisons have no Apcin arm and cannot establish drug restoration of CDC20, BUB1B or hepatic function genes. No drug target engagement, BUBR1/checkpoint correction, Apcin-only healthy control or long-term safety assessment is provided. Credit this organ-level pretreatment signal alongside the context-specific negative findings; it does not establish post-injury treatment, MVA benefit or a clinical therapeutic window.

decisions.disposition: conditional muscle-function research reserve; do not replace current primary comparison
decisions.bub1b_variant_efficacy: Not established for Leu737Ter/Asn1002Lys; no selected experiment administered fisetin to a BUBR1-deficient or MVA model. The reserve is held because the saved reviews report that p16-positive fibro-adipogenic progenitors accumulate in BubR1-insufficient mice and that genetic p16 inactivation there attenuated loss of muscle mass and strength, the same FAP lesion fisetin acted on in Zmpste24-deficient muscle. That is a review's secondhand account of transgenic clearance, not an administered drug and not primary evidence here: it motivates the reserve and supplies no efficacy.
decisions.evidence_scope: Administered fisetin improves distinct whole-animal mouse function measures; progeria co-culture supports a muscle-niche mechanism.
decisions.rationale: Administered dose, 2025 aging study: fisetin 100 mg/kg/day by oral gavage, one week on / two weeks off / one week on, with functional testing about two weeks after the last dose. The Methods print 50 mg/kg/day, but that paragraph is a near-verbatim reuse of the same group's Mahoney 2024 cohort description (100 mg/kg/day, same vehicle, same schedule, same group sizes), 50 mg/kg/day is this paper's ABT-263 dose, and Figure 1A states 100. Treat 100 mg/kg/day as administered and the Methods value as a transcription error; the 2025 muscle outcomes are a new readout on the 2024 cohort, not an independent replication of it. Progeria arm: Zmpste24-deficient mice dosed from 4 months of age with fisetin 100 mg/kg by oral gavage once weekly for 4 weeks (four doses; 10 mg/mL stock in 10% ethanol / 90% PEG-400); controls were Zmpste24-deficient mice given the same volume of that vehicle, with the volume not stated in the source. That is a far lower weekly exposure, in a different vehicle, than the 2025 regimen, and the whole-animal strength gain came from four oral doses. Fisetin improved mean holding impulse in those mice (Figure 5B, p<0.01, n=6) in a study reporting no randomization and no blinding, using a hang test scored from the single longest trial and multiplied by body weight. Normalized forelimb grip improved in old mice (3.30 versus 2.90 g force/g body weight, p=0.0038, n=30 per group; the same arm is n=39 for frailty, with the 9-animal gap unexplained). Absolute force was not measured, but Table 2 shows no fisetin effect on soleus, gastrocnemius, tibialis anterior or quadriceps mass, so this is force per unit mass and not a mass rescue. The two animal endpoints depend on body weight in opposite directions (progeria impulse multiplies by it, aging grip divides by it), so no single body-weight artifact explains both. The 2025 study randomized, matched baseline body weight and blinded data collection; the 2022 progeria study did neither. Selective clearance is demonstrated in vitro only: 20 micromolar fisetin raised TUNEL-positive apoptosis in Zmpste24-deficient fibro-adipogenic progenitors but not wild-type ones, with wild-type progenitor and wild-type FAP control arms. In vivo only marker counts on sections were measured, so what was actually cleared is unknown, and selectivity is untested in aneuploid tissue, where the senescent compartment may be the aneuploid cells this patient depends on. That specific question, not a generic unknown, is what an MVA research test must measure. An FDA-IND phase I/II randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled knee-osteoarthritis trial (74 randomized: 34 fisetin, 40 placebo; oral fisetin 20 mg/kg/day for 2 consecutive days per cycle, 3 cycles, 28 days off) found no between-group benefit on 6-minute walk, 40-metre walk, timed-up-and-go, isokinetic knee strength, gait kinetics, pain, patient-reported outcomes or cartilage T2 (all p>0.05), with no change over time in either arm. Its primary endpoint was 12-month safety and it found no adverse-event difference (185 adverse events; 4 serious, 2 per arm, all unrelated surgeries). Read that as a 12-month randomized adult safety dataset with no efficacy signal at low intermittent exposure in a non-declining population, not as evidence against benefit where a muscle deficit exists, and not as pediatric safety.

decisions.bub1b_variant_efficacy: Not established. No selected administered-combination experiment uses a BUBR1/MVA model.
decisions.evidence_scope: Isolated EDL specific-force result plus separate old-female normalized-grip result, with no demonstrated mass rescue.
decisions.rationale: The actual gavaged mixture (dasatinib 5 mg/kg plus quercetin 50 mg/kg, 3 consecutive days every 15 days for 7 months) improves isolated extensor digitorum longus force in female Sod1-knockout mice. Maximal force (Figure 5A) and specific force (Figure 5B) both show a significant genotype-by-treatment interaction favouring the knockout (p=0.0334 and p=0.0016, two-way ANOVA); only the specific-force panel carries a Tukey post hoc bracket between Sod1KO-vehicle and Sod1KO-D+Q. Absolute force moves in the same direction but is not separately significant within the knockout, so credit specific force and treat absolute force as directionally consistent and unconfirmed; the authors call it modest protection in specific force generation. A separate study normalized grip in aged females. Neither rescued muscle mass, and the Sod1KO study rescued neither neuromuscular-junction fragmentation nor motor-neuron number. Both administered-combination muscle results are female-only: no male arm was tested in either study, and the aging paper's own marker data are sex-divergent (p16 higher in old males, p21 higher in old females) with the intervention run only in females. Male transfer is untested, not established. Neither selected study included a dasatinib-only or quercetin-only arm, so neither component inherits the result and synergy is untested. The quercetin actually administered in the human trial is a specific phytosome product, and no saved source supports equivalence of arbitrary quercetin products. A 12-person phase I, single-blind, single-centre placebo-controlled pilot (6 per arm, 9 doses over 3 weeks) was powered for feasibility and tolerability, not efficacy, and its exploratory function measures in fact favoured placebo (grip +1.8 versus +7.7 kg; 6-minute walk -6.4 versus +16.6 m; between-group 95% confidence intervals -1.6 to 13.4 and -1.0 to 46.9) in a D+Q arm with worse baseline forced vital capacity and less antifibrotic use. The only human muscle-function readout for this combination is null-to-unfavourable and confounded, not merely absent. Tolerability: 65 non-serious adverse-event reports in the D+Q arm versus 22 on placebo (event counts, not patient counts; 25 versus 4 graded severe), with no serious adverse event attributed to D+Q and no myelosuppression observed. The FDA label establishes pediatric dosing from 1 year of age (weight-banded, 40 to 100 mg once daily), with pharmacokinetics in 43 children and 97 chronic-phase CML children treated a median 51.1 months, so pediatric exposure at senolytic-relevant daily doses is characterized; what is missing is any intermittent, non-oncology schedule in children. The label's pediatric-specific hazard is skeletal: bone growth and development reactions in 5 of 97 (5.2%) after at least 2 years of continuous dosing, one Grade 3 growth retardation, plus delayed epiphyseal fusion and osteopenia, and no data below 1 year. No pediatric MVA senolytic window is established, and the growth-plate signal is the specific risk to weigh for a growing child. No BUBR1 or chromosome-fidelity rescue is demonstrated; retain a combination-only reserve.

decisions.route: UMK57 / MCAK potentiation and chromosome-segregation fidelity
decisions.disposition: mechanistic fidelity lead with acute benefit; durability and model-transfer constraints; no clinical nomination
decisions.bub1b_variant_efficacy: Not established. No BUB1B-hypomorphic, MVA, or patient-specific deficient cell was tested.
decisions.evidence_scope: Human cancer-cell acute lagging-chromosome reduction and one-chromosome post-cytokinesis mis-segregation reduction; no muscle or in-vivo therapeutic result. Complete main text, methods and all four main figures reviewed; supplementary results identified separately.
decisions.rationale: At 100 nM against 0.1% DMSO, UMK57 potentiates MCAK-dependent microtubule depolymerization and reduces acute lagging anaphases in U2OS, HeLa and SW-620; inactive UMK95 and MCAK-depletion controls support the proposed mechanism. Figure 2B reports n>300 anaphases and three independent experiments. Figure 2D also reports a significant reduction in total mis-segregation of one tagged chromosome among >600 daughter-nucleus pairs after 15 h monastrol arrest, washout and 8 h recovery. This credits a completed-division outcome, not all-chromosome faithful daughter yield per starting cell. Figure 2H does measure kinetochore BubR1 normalized to Hec1 (>=150 kinetochores from 10-20 cells), without a significant acute change; it does not show total BUBR1 restoration. Attachment half-life measurements use 5 micromolar MG132 and must be kept separate from the completed-division assay. The significant early lagging-chromosome benefit is no longer significant at 72 h in all three cancer lines; two U2OS single-cell colonies per condition show no reduction in chromosome 2/3 modal-copy heterogeneity after 6-8 weeks. These are context-limited durability negatives, not proof that any effect must be exactly zero or that every clinical schedule would fail. Figure 4E credits 250 nM ZM447439 plus UMK57 with benefit persisting to 72 h in U2OS, lost by 96 h; running text reports a similar delay in SW-620 and no delay in HeLa, whose supplementary panels were not independently viewed. Persistent metaphase attachment destabilization is consistent with continued pharmacodynamic activity, not direct target occupancy. High-dose prometaphase accumulation and increased spindle/alignment defects with MCAK overexpression are observed context-dependent harms. No growing-animal force, BUBR1-deficient rescue, clinical exposure or pediatric safety result was established. Absence from the checked catalog is not proof of absent clinical existence. Preserve the positive as a mechanistic lead; neither extrapolate it to MVA nor convert the cancer-cell durability result into a class-wide contraindication. It does not currently displace niacin restoration or apitegromab compensation, neither of which is MVA-proven. Figure 2B also includes non-transformed, hTERT-immortalized RPE-1 and BJ cells: neither shows a statistically significant change in lagging-anaphase frequency at 100 nM, with low baseline rates. RPE-1 single-cell colonies grown for 4-6 weeks also retain low chromosome 2/3 copy-number heterogeneity. These restricted null results bound the tested models; they do not establish inactivity in every non-cancer cell or in genetically affected MVA cells. Reported 12%/9.8% strength gains are within-arm percentages, while placebo declined about 9-10%; they are not adjusted treatment-effect percentages. Peak-power primary was null; walking/peak-VO2 comparisons were nonsignificant despite within-arm gains. Numeric adjusted 95% clinical contrast CIs were not provided in examined sources. Neither is significant at 26 weeks; no treatment-by-time test establishes waning. Multiplicity, steroid imbalance 12/23 versus 21/24, 43 complete primary cases among 45 study completers, source reporting conflicts and 3 active-arm severe events including 2 fall-associated fractures limit confirmation and safety inference. It does not currently displace the recorded apitegromab pediatric SMA primary functional evidence.
